sections.overview: This southern African bottom-dwelling fish belongs to Congiopodidae, a family often called horsefishes or pigfishes.
sections.identification: Its compressed, rough-skinned body has a protruding snout with strong spines and a brown, dark-spotted pattern.
sections.habitat: It lives off southern Africa from Walvis Bay to KwaZulu-Natal, over rocky reefs and sandy bottoms.
sections.diet: It feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates, including crustaceans, molluscs, sea urchins, brittle stars and worms.
sections.behavior: It is demersal and often caught incidentally by bottom trawlers; aquarium observations suggest greater activity at night.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive details were not available in the regional identification and aquarium sources consulted.
sections.ecology: It is readily distinguished from the smooth horsefish, Congiopodus torvus, by the spined snout and rough skin.
sections.conservation: The aquarium account does not consider it threatened, but notes pollution and trawl bycatch among potential pressures.
